speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Minister for Health whether the Ministry can guide the elderly through public education on how to spot signs and symptoms of an impending dizzy spell so that they can prevent a fall and causing injury to themselves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Seniors fall due to many reasons such as giddiness and loss of muscle strength.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: MOH and the Health Promotion Board (HPB) have been working with community partners and healthcare clusters to raise awareness on falls prevention through public education, exercise programmes and campaigns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Under the National Seniors' Health Programme, regular health talks and workshops are conducted at various community touchpoints to educate seniors on falls prevention.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Seniors on long-term medication for several medical conditions are also advised to consult a doctor for a medication review at least once a year, as a possible side effect of taking multiple medications concurrently includes dizziness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Seniors are encouraged to exercise regularly, and to do strength, balance and flexibility exercises at least twice a week.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: This helps to delay age-related loss of muscle mass and strength, which reduces the risk of falls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: The HPB also piloted "Rolling Good Times" in 2018, a programme to raise awareness of common falls situations, improve seniors' strength and balance through exercises, and teach them how to minimise the risk of injuries during a fall.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Hence, HPB intends to reach out to more seniors by progressively rolling out the programme to more community nodes nationwide.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Targeting pre-frail and frail seniors, the Healthy Ageing Promotion Programme For You (HAPPY) programme implemented by the National University Health System engages seniors in exercises combined with cognitive activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Such dual-task exercises have been shown to stimulate cognitive functions and improve physical ability, preventing dementia and frailty as well as reducing one's risk for falls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Although senior-centric activities have been temporarily suspended since March 2020 due to COVID-19, many organisations have since adapted most of their activities and classes to online content so that our seniors can continue to stay active and engaged while at home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Lastly, HPB had organised Falls Prevention Awareness campaigns in 2016 and 2017 to provide seniors and their care-givers with information on how to reduce the risk of falls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: As part of the campaigns, educational videos and guidebooks were produced for seniors and their care-givers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Health)
text: MOH and the healthcare family will continue to strengthen our efforts to reduce the risk of falls among our senior population.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Many elderly fall at home and sometimes their families did not even realise till after some time.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: For those who live alone, it could be an even longer lag time before someone discovered the elderly had fallen.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: With this in mind, may I ask how MOH or perhaps HPB can deploy more wearable fall detection alarm devices for elderly, especially those who have been assessed by medical professionals to have a higher risk of falling and perhaps even those who live alone.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: First, let me say that for seniors living alone, we have, for instance, our Silver Generation Ambassadors, who call or visit them to check on them and see how they are doing.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We also work with other Community Partners and VWOs to check on these seniors.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Indeed, we are also looking at various ways to detect falls and then raise the alarm to the community either at the Senior Activity Centre or to other various partners.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There are actually many commercial wearable devices and products that can help to detect falls and then trigger an alarm for assistance should the wearer fall and these are useful for detecting falls, especially for seniors with higher risk of falling.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, this trial is one of the Internet of Things initiative under the Smart Nation Sensor platform.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is really to enable us to get feedback from the user on this prototype to see how we can develop, design and develop a cost-effective, lightweight as well as easily deployable personal alert button system.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: What is also important is that actually for all these variables and these personal alert systems, you trigger an alarm for assistance after the fall, after the seniors have fallen.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In fact, what we want to do is to proactively prevent occurrence of such falls as much as possible.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, the best strategy still is really to focus upstream on falls prevention, pre-empting the falls, addressing the risk of falling through our multi-pronged effort which I have actually highlighted in terms of falls prevention, awareness programmes, getting the seniors to exercise regularly, especially to improve strength, balance, flexibility, nutrition to maintain or reduce or delay the loss of muscle mass and to build strong bones as well as getting rid of clutter in the homes and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We have also worked with Mediacorp to launch Season two of "乐学每疫刻" or "Learn Together With Me", which started just yesterday and will last till the 15 May, Monday to Friday 2.30 pm to 3.00 pm, for the seniors who are interested.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: That includes talks as well as exercise programmes to help the seniors remain active and healthy.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It will also be shown on Suria and Vasantham after Channel 8, so I would encourage you to get the seniors to also view this.
